4.1 What does the research say?

4.1.1 OKC

The training program may include both low/no-load full ROM leg extension as well as ROM-restricted leg extension when the patient is able to lift heavier loads. Minimal ACL strain and reduced PFJ reaction forces have been observed during quadriceps contractions performed between 45-90º of knee flexion, and therefore this is the recommended ROM for loading to be introduced [1].

Early introduction of isometrics is recommended ?

Leg Ext isometrics between 90-60º (5x45s, 1-2x per day)

Full ROM (90-0º) against gravity/low loads can be performed once able to comfortably achieve 90º knee flexion

Restricted ROM loaded knee extensions may begin 4 weeks post ACLR (Tempo 3:03, 15-25RM loads)

4.2 Testing

Each card below contains a detailed description of the tests to be conducted during this phase of rehab.

4.2.1 Pistol Squat

Full range of motion single leg squats while standing on a box.

  • The athlete stands on a box that is high enough to let their opposite leg hang to the side and not touch the ground in the bottom of the squat. For a repetition to be succesful, the angle of the knee joint must exceed 90 degrees. Practitioner discretion is crucial to determine proper technique. If there is excessive frontal plan motion (i.e. knee valgus) or excessive hip lift (off-loading the quads), consider carefully whether reps should be counted towards succesful achievment of this criteria.

Criteria: ≥ 5

4.2.2 Quad Strength

Isometric Strength at 90°

  • Seated with hip and knees flexed at 90°. Dynamometer placed on the anterior aspect of the shank, proximal to the ankle joint. Target score to complete this phase is 75% LSI compared to un-injured leg.

Criteria: > 95%

Repetitions: 3

Calculation: Max

4.2.3 Hamstring Strength

Isometric Strength at 90°

  • Seated with hip and knees flexed at 90°. Dynamometer placed on the anterior aspect of the shank, proximal to the ankle joint. Target score to complete this phase is 75% LSI compared to un-injured leg.

Criteria: > 95%

Repetitions: 3

Calculation: Max

4.2.4 CMJ Height

Scores are relative to baseline data

  • Height in cm

Criteria: ≥ 95%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean

4.2.5 CMJ RSImod

Scores are relative to baseline data

  • Height of jump divided by total contraction time

Criteria: ≥ 95%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean

4.2.6 CMJ Lengthening Asymmetry

Confidence interval around the mean of 5 jumps must be entirely within ± 10%

  • Ratio of force produced by each limb in the lengthening (lowering) phase of the jump

Criteria: < 10%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean ± CI

4.2.7 CMJ Lengthening Impulse

Scores are relative to baseline data

  • Phase impulse is tracked independently to ensure that ratio data does not represent a drop in force production of the non-injured limb.

Criteria: ≥ 95%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean

4.2.8 CMJ Shortening Asymmetry

Confidence interval around the mean of 5 jumps must be entirely within ± 10%

  • Ratio of force produced by each limb in the shortening (propulsive) phase of the jump

Criteria: < 10%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean ± CI

4.2.9 CMJ Shortening Impulse

Scores are relative to baseline data

  • Phase impulse is tracked independently to ensure that ratio data does not represent a drop in force production of the non-injured limb.

Criteria: ≥ 95%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean

4.2.10 Drop and Stick - Time to Stabilization

Time taken to return the body to a stable state following a 50cm drop landing.

  • Participant steps forward off 50cm box with their preferred leg and lands on the force plates in a squat with thighs parallel to the floor and arms held out ion front of them.
    Cue: “Land softly and stabilize as quickly as possible” TTS target scores are based off old research for now.

Criteria: < 0.75s

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean

4.2.11 Drop and Stick - Landing Force

The amount of force required to bring the body to a stable state following a 50cm drop landing.

  • Participant steps forward off 50cm box with their preferred leg and lands on the force plates in a squat with thighs parallel to the floor and arms held out ion front of them.
    Cue: “Land softly and stabilize as quickly as possible” rPLF target scores are based off old research for now.

Criteria: < 3.5x BM

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean

4.2.12 Drop and Stick - Landing Asymmetry

Confidence interval around the mean of 5 jumps must be entirely within ± 10%

  • Participant steps forward off 50cm box with their preferred leg and lands on the force plates in a squat with thighs parallel to the floor and arms held out ion front of them.
    Cue: “Land softly and stabilize as quickly as possible” rPLF target scores are based off old research for now.

Criteria: < 15%

Repetitions: 5

Calculation: Mean ± CI

4.4.1 Blood Flow Restriction

Although, blood flow restrictio

Another more recent study did not report how early BFR began after surgery, but did use the following criteria to begin BFR: able to stand on one leg unsupported for >5s, knee ROM between 0-90º, able to perform SLR with sufficient quadriceps activation [2] . Patients performed the traditional 30-15-15-15 reps of leg press

4.5 Notes and Considerations for Reviewers

All feedback is welcome, however here are some considerations that should help inform the development of this tool.

Components of MRSS2.0:
1. Clinical Examination (10 pts)
2. IKDC + ACL-RSI (20 pts)
3. Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia (hurdle)
4. Functional Testing (50 pts)
5. General Fitness (hurdle)
6. Functional Testing in Fatigued State (20 pts)
